title: Hidden Windows launcher makes native startup failures look like an unexplained flash-exit
summary: Quick-Automatic-Hardsub-Encoder's normal Windows entry point starts native-bridge.ps1 with PowerShell -WindowStyle Hidden and immediately exits the batch process. Most bridge startup exceptions are therefore invisible to the user; only the explicit missing-FFmpeg branch has a MessageBox. On a real Windows machine the reported symptom is that the Windows version 'flashes and exits'. The root startup exception is not yet identified, but the launcher/diagnostic behavior is independently defective because it collapses distinct startup failures into the same silent symptom. Preserve the hidden-background UX on success, but on startup failure emit a durable log and visible error with a debug/retry path.

evidence.user_report: Windows version flashes and exits immediately on the user's machine.
evidence.launcher: windows/start_windows.bat uses start powershell.exe ... -WindowStyle Hidden -File native-bridge.ps1, then exit /b 0.
evidence.debug_path: windows/start_windows_debug.bat runs the same bridge visibly and pauses on non-zero exit.
evidence.code_observation: native-bridge.ps1 handles missing FFmpeg with a MessageBox, but other top-level startup exceptions are not wrapped in a visible failure path.
